column2: Early Results on Monitorability in QA Settings
column6: Qualifying empirical/methodology findings: monitor evasion rates measured (GPT-4o-mini fooled 46.5%, GPT-4o/Claude Sonnet ~22-24%), RL-trained 8B model fooled GPT-4o-mini monitor, evasion correlated with side-task reasoning difficulty

column2: MALT: A Dataset of Natural and Prompted Behaviors That Threaten Eval Integrity
column6: Qualifying methodology/empirical findings: 10,919-transcript labeled dataset with 103 unprompted reward-hacking examples; monitor AUROC 0.96 (reward hacking) and 0.91 (sandbagging); 80-90% TPR at 5% FPR

column2: Summary of our gpt-oss methodology review
column6: Qualifying governance/process findings from METR's own review of OpenAI's gpt-oss-120b malicious fine-tuning methodology: OpenAI adopted 9 of METR's 17 recommendations incl. 5 high-urgency; High-capability classification criteria only partially addressed (internal thresholds not published)

column2: Review of the Anthropic Summer 2025 Pilot Sabotage Risk Report
column6: Qualifying governance/process findings from METR's independent review: agrees catastrophic sabotage risk from Claude Opus 4/4.1 is low but finds Claim 2 lacks task-type precision and Anthropic possibly overconfident on monitoring reliability; distinct from the later Opus 4.6 review (METR-2026-03-OPUS46SABOTAGE)

Qualifying empirical model findings: 50% time horizon ~2h40m and 80% ~30m for GPT-5.1-Codex-Max across 170 tasks; failed all five attempts at two manually-scored long-horizon tasks; assessed low-risk incremental improvement. Matches dataset report METR-2025-11-GPT51CODEXMAX

column2: Common Elements of Frontier AI Safety Policies (December 2025 Update)
column6: Descriptive policy-comparison resource cataloguing commonalities across twelve companies' safety policies (update of Aug/Nov 2024 and Mar 2025 versions); no measured results or evaluation findings asserted by METR

Qualifying empirical findings from new SHUSHCAST evaluation prototype (distinct from Oct 2025 QA note): reasoning-trace access raised monitor catch rates on GPT-5 agents by >50pp; agent/monitor time-horizon ratio predicts evasion success

Author clarification/opinion note on interpreting the time horizon metric (definition, ~2x error bars, domain variation); restates prior time horizon paper results and presents no new evidence-backed findings

column2: Frontier AI safety regulations: A reference for lab staff
column6: Reference/explainer synthesizing legal requirements of SB 53, EU CoP, RAISE Act and Illinois SB 315 for lab staff; regulatory summary with no measured results or evaluation findings

Qualifying empirical/methodology findings: re-estimated time horizons for 14 models on expanded 228-task suite under Inspect; since-2023 doubling time 131 days (20% faster than TH1); GPT-5 estimate +55%, GPT-4 variants -35-57%; Vivaria vs Inspect infrastructure comparison

column2: A simpler AI timelines model predicts 99% AI R&D automation in ~2032
column6: Forecasting/modeling exercise: 8-parameter simulation projecting ~2032 automation; outputs are projections from assumed parameters (author calls them educated guesses), not evidence-backed measured findings

column2: Measuring Time Horizon using Claude Code and Codex
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: specialized scaffolds did not beat defaults (Claude Code beats ReAct in 50.7% of bootstraps for Opus 4.5; Codex beats Triframe in 14.5% for GPT-5); observed behaviors incl. GPT-5/Codex poor situational awareness and Opus 4.5 plan over-anchoring

column2: Analyzing coding agent transcripts to upper bound productivity gains from AI agents
column6: Qualifying empirical/methodology findings: analysis of 5,305 Claude Code transcripts from 7 staff gives soft-upper-bound time savings of ~1.5x-13x; higher agent concurrency correlates with higher savings; ~27% of AI-assisted work would not otherwise have occurred

Explainer of METR's own internal confidentiality/security practices (six-tier classification, codenames, SOC 2 Type I); organizational self-description with no evaluation findings about any model or evaluation process

column2: Five lessons from having helped run an AI-Biology RCT
column6: Lessons-learned/opinion piece; the empirical results it cites (153-novice RCT, no significant end-to-end uplift) restate the Active Site (formerly Panoplia Laboratories) RCT main-results publication, which is the primary source; the five lessons themselves are recommendations, not findings

column2: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
column6: Qualifying methodology/process findings: documented selection effects invalidating the late-2025 uplift RCT (developers refused AI-disallowed participation; 30-50% withheld AI-suitable tasks; concurrent-agent time tracking unreliable), rendering the -18%/-4% speedup estimates only very weak evidence

column2: Observations from two CLI game reimplementation runs with Opus 4.6
column6: Qualifying empirical model findings (observed behaviour): Claude Opus 4.6 produced mostly-playable but buggy CLI reimplementations of Slay the Spire and Balatro, work estimated at 2-8 weeks of human developer time, exceeding researcher expectations

column2: Many SWE-bench-Passing PRs Would Not Be Merged into Main
column6: Qualifying empirical/methodology findings: maintainer review of 296 test-passing SWE-bench Verified PRs (Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet, Claude 4 Opus, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, GPT-5) found acceptance ~24pp below automated grader scores; roughly half would not be merged; ~50% of human golden-patch baseline
